1	"""A business question: the specification, the acceptance test and what a page renders.
     2	
     3	It is a data file rather than code, which is what keeps the vocabulary of one business out
     4	of the machinery that runs it. The runner discovers questions and asserts over them; it
     5	names nothing. ADR 0005.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import json
    11	import re
    12	from dataclasses import dataclass
    13	from enum import StrEnum
    14	from pathlib import Path
    15	from typing import Any
    16	
    17	import duckdb
    18	import yaml
    19	
    20	FRONT_MATTER = re.compile(r"\A---\n(.*?)\n---\n(.*)\Z", re.DOTALL)
    21	TOKEN = re.compile(r"\{\{([^}]+)\}\}")
    22	
    23	STAGED = "staged.sql"
    24	USS = "uss.sql"
    25	
    26	# The prefix every bridge measure column carries, as a literal beside the layer names
    27	# below. Generated by adss.uss; a test asserts the two still agree, which is the coupling
    28	# without the import -- a question is a data file and does not depend on a generator.
    29	MEASURE = "_measure__"
    30	
    31	
    32	ID = re.compile(r"\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*\Z")
    33	
    34	
    35	class QuestionError(Exception):
    36	    """A question that cannot be answered as written."""
    37	
    38	
    39	class Status(StrEnum):
    40	    DRAFT = "draft"
    41	    RED = "red"
    42	    GREEN = "green"
    43	    SUPERSEDED = "superseded"
    44	
    45	
    46	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    47	class Question:
    48	    directory: Path
    49	    id: str
    50	    status: Status
    51	    persona: str
    52	    question: str
    53	    dimensions: tuple[str, ...]
    54	    defines: tuple[str, ...]
    55	    staged_sql: str
    56	    uss_sql: str
    57	    body: str
    58	
    59	    @property
    60	    def tokens(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    61	        return tuple(str(match).strip() for match in TOKEN.findall(self.body))
    62	
    63	
    64	def without_comments(sql: str) -> str:
    65	    """The SQL, without its commentary. A comment explaining a rule does not break it."""
    66	    return "\n".join(line for line in sql.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("--"))
    67	
    68	
    69	def _parsed(sql: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    70	    """The engine's own parse tree for this SQL, as plain data.
    71	
    72	    Parsed rather than matched. An aggregate can be spelled over three lines, wrapped in a
    73	    cast, or written as a window, and a regular expression that survived all three would still
    74	    be reading string literals and comments as code.
    75	    """
    76	    tree: dict[str, Any] = {"error": True, "error_message": "the engine returned nothing"}
    77	    connection = duckdb.connect(":memory:")
    78	    try:
    79	        found = connection.execute("SELECT json_serialize_sql(?)", [sql]).fetchone()
    80	        if found:
    81	            tree = json.loads(str(found[0]))
    82	    finally:
    83	        connection.close()
    84	    return tree
    85	
    86	
    87	def _aggregate_names() -> frozenset[str]:
    88	    """Every aggregate the engine has, from the engine. A list kept by hand here would be
    89	    wrong the first time somebody wrote `product` or `arg_max` instead of `sum`."""
    90	    connection = duckdb.connect(":memory:")
    91	    try:
    92	        rows = connection.execute(
    93	            "SELECT DISTINCT function_name FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE function_type = ?",
    94	            ["aggregate"],
    95	        ).fetchall()
    96	    finally:
    97	        connection.close()
    98	    return frozenset(str(name).lower() for (name,) in rows)
    99	
   100	
   101	def _columns_under(node: object) -> list[str]:
   102	    """Every column named anywhere below this node, qualifier and all."""
   103	    if isinstance(node, dict):
   104	        if node.get("class") == "COLUMN_REF":
   105	            names = node.get("column_names")
   106	            parts = names if isinstance(names, list) else []
   107	            return [".".join(str(part) for part in parts)]
   108	        return [found for value in node.values() for found in _columns_under(value)]
   109	    if isinstance(node, list):
   110	        return [found for value in node for found in _columns_under(value)]
   111	    return []
   112	
   113	
   114	def aggregated(
   115	    tree: dict[str, Any], aggregates: frozenset[str]
   116	) -> list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]]:
   117	    """Every aggregate in this parse tree, with the columns it is applied to.
   118	
   119	    A windowed aggregate counts: `sum(x) OVER ()` multiplies exactly as a grouped sum does.
   120	    An aggregate with no columns at all -- `count(*)` -- comes back with none, which is a
   121	    different refusal rather than an absent one.
   122	    """
   123	    found: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
   124	
   125	    def walk(node: object) -> None:
   126	        if isinstance(node, list):
   127	            for value in node:
   128	                walk(value)
   129	            return
   130	        if not isinstance(node, dict):
   131	            return
   132	        name = str(node.get("function_name", "")).lower()
   133	        aggregate = node.get("class") in ("FUNCTION", "WINDOW") and not node.get("is_operator")
   134	        if aggregate and name in aggregates:
   135	            found.append((name, tuple(_columns_under(node.get("children", [])))))
   136	        for value in node.values():
   137	            walk(value)
   138	
   139	    walk(tree.get("statements"))
   140	    return found
   141	
   142	
   143	def _refuse_an_aggregate_the_bridge_does_not_protect(
   144	    question: Question, tree: dict[str, Any]
   145	) -> None:
   146	    """An answer query aggregates measures and nothing else. ADR 0012.
   147	
   148	    The bridge protects a measure column with a typed null on every branch that does not own
   149	    it. It protects nothing on a peripheral, and a numeric attribute that is also a measure's
   150	    source is published in both places -- so one join and one sum returns a multiple of the
   151	    truth, looking exactly like an answer.
   152	
   153	    Stricter than the trap strictly requires: `count(DISTINCT p.thing)` cannot be multiplied
   154	    by a fan-out, and is refused here anyway. The decision is that an answer aggregates
   155	    measures, and narrowing it to the aggregates that can actually be wrong would be a rule
   156	    nobody could apply without knowing which those are.
   157	    """
   158	    for name, columns in aggregated(tree, _aggregate_names()):
   159	        if not columns:
   160	            raise QuestionError(
   161	                f"{question.id}: the answer query says {name}() over no column, which counts "
   162	                f"measurement events rather than the thing anybody asked about -- two events "
   163	                f"on one entity and it doubles. Sum the measure that counts them instead."
   164	            )
   165	        loose = [column for column in columns if MEASURE not in column]
   166	        if loose:
   167	            raise QuestionError(
   168	                f"{question.id}: the answer query applies {name}() to {loose}, which the "
   169	                f"bridge does not protect. A numeric attribute on a peripheral is published "
   170	                f"beside the measure made from it and multiplies once per row of the finer "
   171	                f"stage. Aggregate the {MEASURE} column instead. ADR 0012."
   172	            )
   173	
   174	
   175	def read_question(directory: Path) -> Question:
   176	    text = (directory / "question.md").read_text()
   177	    parsed = FRONT_MATTER.match(text)
   178	    if parsed is None:
   179	        raise QuestionError(f"{directory}: question.md has no front matter")
   180	    front = yaml.safe_load(parsed.group(1))
   181	    # The id becomes a file name and an environment variable, so it may not be empty, contain a
   182	    # separator, or be anything a shell or a path would read as more than a name. An empty one
   183	    # is the worst of them: it means "every question" to the page, so the record of what was
   184	    # delivered for this question would quietly be a picture of all of them.
   185	    identifier = str(front["id"])
   186	    if not ID.match(identifier):
   187	        raise QuestionError(
   188	            f"{directory}: {identifier!r} is not a usable question id. It names a file and an "
   189	            f"environment variable, so it must be lower-case letters, digits, hyphen and "
   190	            f"underscore, and must not be empty."
   191	        )
   192	    return Question(
   193	        directory=directory,
   194	        id=identifier,
   195	        status=Status(str(front["status"])),
   196	        persona=str(front["persona"]),
   197	        question=str(front["question"]),
   198	        dimensions=tuple(str(d) for d in front["dimensions"]),
   199	        defines=tuple(str(d) for d in front["defines"]),
   200	        staged_sql=(directory / STAGED).read_text(),
   201	        uss_sql=(directory / USS).read_text(),
   202	        body=parsed.group(2),
   203	    )
   204	
   205	
   206	def read_questions(root: Path) -> tuple[Question, ...]:
   207	    return tuple(
   208	        read_question(directory)
   209	        for directory in sorted(root.iterdir())
   210	        if (directory / "question.md").is_file()
   211	    )
   212	
   213	
   214	def check_question(question: Question, defined: dict[str, str]) -> None:
   215	    """Refuse a question that cannot be answered, or answered honestly."""
   216	    for token in question.tokens:
   217	        if token not in defined:
   218	            raise QuestionError(
   219	                f"{question.id}: {{{{{token}}}}} resolves to nothing. A question references "
   220	                f"definitions and never restates one, so a token with no definition behind "
   221	                f"it is a gap in the model -- fill it there first."
   222	            )
   223	    missing = [name for name in question.defines if name not in defined]
   224	    if missing:
   225	        raise QuestionError(f"{question.id}: declares {missing}, which nothing defines")
   226	
   227	    control = without_comments(question.staged_sql).lower()
   228	    for forbidden in ("dab.", "dab__", "dar__uss"):
   229	        if forbidden in control:
   230	            raise QuestionError(
   231	                f"{question.id}: the control query mentions {forbidden!r}. It must compute "
   232	                f"the answer independently, or agreement between the two proves nothing."
   233	            )
   234	    if "das__staged." not in control or "__current" not in control:
   235	        raise QuestionError(
   236	            f"{question.id}: the control query must read a das__staged __current view. "
   237	            f"Reading the raw layer or the lake skips the contract's casts, which is what "
   238	            f"makes agreement mean anything."
   239	        )
   240	
   241	    answer = without_comments(question.uss_sql).lower()
   242	    parsed = _parsed(answer)
   243	    if parsed.get("error"):
   244	        raise QuestionError(
   245	            f"{question.id}: the answer query does not parse -- "
   246	            f"{parsed.get('error_message', 'the engine did not say why')}. Refused here rather "
   247	            f"than at the next build, after a page has been written against it."
   248	        )
   249	    if "dar__uss" not in answer:
   250	        raise QuestionError(f"{question.id}: the answer query does not read the star schema")
   251	    for forbidden in ("das__", "dab.", "dab__", "read_parquet"):
   252	        if forbidden in answer:
   253	            raise QuestionError(
   254	                f"{question.id}: the answer query mentions {forbidden!r}. A destination reads "
   255	                f"the star schema and nothing else -- the page runs this query verbatim, so a "
   256	                f"reach past it would render, pass, and be exactly the invisible dependency "
   257	                f"the flow rules exist to prevent."
   258	            )
   259	
   260	    for body, side in ((control, "control"), (answer, "answer")):
   261	        if "order by" not in body:
   262	            raise QuestionError(
   263	                f"{question.id}: the {side} query has no ORDER BY. The two answers are "
   264	                f"compared row by row, so without one an identical pair can differ by the "
   265	                f"order the engine happened to return, and someone goes looking for a data "
   266	                f"bug that is not there."
   267	            )
   268	
   269	    # Only the answer query. The control expresses the same dimension in the source's own
   270	    # words -- that difference is what makes it independent rather than a transcription.
   271	    for dimension in question.dimensions:
   272	        if dimension.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() not in answer:
   273	            raise QuestionError(
   274	                f"{question.id}: declares the dimension {dimension!r}, which the answer query "
   275	                f"does not mention. The front matter is what a reader trusts."
   276	            )
   277	
   278	    _refuse_an_aggregate_the_bridge_does_not_protect(question, parsed)

+    directory = tmp_path / name

+    """ADR 0012. The bridge protects the measure column and not the attribute beside it.

+    One join and one sum, which is the shape every question here already writes -- and over a
+    bridge with two rows per order it returns twice the truth with nothing to show for it.

1	"""A parent's measure is not multiplied by its children. ADR 0002, ADR 0012, deviation D-0001.
     2	
     3	The whole argument for putting every process in one shared star schema is that a measure cannot
     4	fan out across a walk over many-to-one edges: a key inherits, a measure does not. Slices 1 to 3
     5	could not demonstrate it -- every entity was at one grain, so no measure *could* multiply however
     6	the join was written, and the register said so. This is the shape that can.
     7	
     8	It runs the generated SQL rather than reading it. A substring assertion would pass a generator
     9	that emitted the right typed nulls in the wrong branch, which is exactly the defect this exists
    10	to catch. The warehouse is synthetic and built here, which conventions section 6 permits a
    11	machinery test to do and forbids a data check from doing.
    12	"""
    13	
    14	from decimal import Decimal
    15	from pathlib import Path
    16	
    17	import duckdb
    18	import pytest
    19	
    20	from adss.model import read_model
    21	from adss.uss import bridge_sql, peripheral_sql, read_uss
    22	
    23	FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "dab"
    24	
    25	Db = duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection
    26	
    27	# One parent worth 100.50 and one worth 50.25, and three children between them each worth 5.00.
    28	# If a measure inherited as a key does, the parents' total would be 100.50 x 2 + 50.25 = 251.25
    29	# rather than 150.75 -- which is the shape of every fan-trap bug there is.
    30	PARENTS = [("P1", Decimal("100.50")), ("P2", Decimal("50.25"))]
    31	CHILDREN = [
    32	    ("C1", "P1", Decimal("5.00")),
    33	    ("C2", "P1", Decimal("5.00")),
    34	    ("C3", "P2", Decimal("5.00")),
    35	]
    36	
    37	WHEN = "2026-01-01"
    38	
    39	TOTAL = "SELECT sum(_measure__parent__size_parents_units) FROM dar__uss._bridge"
    40	OCCURRED = "SELECT count(*) FROM dar__uss._bridge WHERE _event = 'occurred'"
    41	
    42	
    43	def _engine_objects(connection: Db) -> None:
    44	    """The objects the generator reads, shaped as the engine shapes them."""
    45	    connection.execute("CREATE SCHEMA dab")
    46	    connection.execute("CREATE SCHEMA dar__uss")
    47	    connection.execute(
    48	        'CREATE TABLE dab."view_PARENT_hist" ("PARENT_key" VARCHAR, eff_tmstp TIMESTAMP, '
    49	        '"PARENT_NUMBER" VARCHAR, "HAPPENED_ON" TIMESTAMP, "PARENT_LABEL" VARCHAR, '
    50	        '"PARENT_SIZE" DECIMAL(28, 8), "FINISHED_ON" TIMESTAMP)'
    51	    )
    52	    connection.execute(
    53	        'CREATE TABLE dab."view_CHILD_hist" ("CHILD_key" VARCHAR, eff_tmstp TIMESTAMP, '
    54	        '"CHILD_NUMBER" VARCHAR, "OCCURRED_ON" TIMESTAMP, "CHILD_WEIGHT" DECIMAL(28, 8))'
    55	    )
    56	    connection.execute(
    57	        'CREATE TABLE dab."view_NEIGHBOUR_hist" ("NEIGHBOUR_key" VARCHAR, eff_tmstp TIMESTAMP, '
    58	        '"NEIGHBOUR_NUMBER" VARCHAR, "NEIGHBOUR_LABEL" VARCHAR)'
    59	    )
    60	    for edge, source, target in (
    61	        ("CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT", "CHILD", "PARENT"),
    62	        ("CHILD_SITS_BESIDE_NEIGHBOUR", "CHILD", "NEIGHBOUR"),
    63	    ):
    64	        connection.execute(
    65	            f'CREATE TABLE dab."v_{edge}" ("{source}_key" VARCHAR, "{target}_key" VARCHAR, '
    66	            f"rel_name VARCHAR, eff_tmstp TIMESTAMP, ver_tmstp TIMESTAMP, row_st VARCHAR)"
    67	        )
    68	
    69	
    70	def _load(connection: Db, children: list[tuple[str, str, Decimal]]) -> None:
    71	    for key, size in PARENTS:
    72	        connection.execute(
    73	            'INSERT INTO dab."view_PARENT_hist" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)',
    74	            [key, WHEN, key, WHEN, key, size],
    75	        )
    76	    for key, parent, weight in children:
    77	        connection.execute(
    78	            'INSERT INTO dab."view_CHILD_hist" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
    79	            [key, WHEN, key, WHEN, weight],
    80	        )
    81	        connection.execute(
    82	            'INSERT INTO dab."v_CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
    83	            [key, parent, "CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT", WHEN, WHEN, "Y"],
    84	        )
    85	
    86	
    87	def _build(connection: Db) -> None:
    88	    model = read_model(FIXTURES / "model.yaml")
    89	    uss = read_uss(FIXTURES / "uss.yaml", model)
    90	    for entity in ("PARENT", "CHILD", "NEIGHBOUR"):
    91	        connection.execute(peripheral_sql(model, entity).replace(";", ""))
    92	    connection.execute(bridge_sql(model, uss).replace(";", ""))
    93	
    94	
    95	def _total(connection: Db, sql: str) -> object:
    96	    found = connection.execute(sql).fetchone()
    97	    assert found is not None
    98	    return found[0]
    99	
   100	
   101	@pytest.fixture
   102	def scratch(tmp_path: Path):
   103	    connection = duckdb.connect(str(tmp_path / "fan.duckdb"))
   104	    _engine_objects(connection)
   105	    _load(connection, CHILDREN)
   106	    _build(connection)
   107	    yield connection
   108	    connection.close()
   109	
   110	
   111	def test_a_parents_measure_is_its_own_total_and_not_its_children_times_it(scratch: Db):
   112	    """150.75, not 251.25. This is the property D-0001 is carried on."""
   113	    assert _total(scratch, TOTAL) == Decimal("150.75")
   114	
   115	
   116	def test_both_grains_are_right_in_one_scan(scratch: Db):
   117	    """The query a reader actually writes, and the one that traps."""
   118	    found = scratch.execute(
   119	        "SELECT sum(_measure__parent__size_parents_units), "
   120	        "sum(_measure__child__weight_children_units), count(*) FROM dar__uss._bridge"
   121	    ).fetchone()
   122	    # Five rows, not six: two parents happened, three children occurred, and neither parent
   123	    # finished -- so that event has no rows at all, which is the absent-event rule turning up
   124	    # here without being asked for.
   125	    assert found == (Decimal("150.75"), Decimal("15.00"), 5)
   126	
   127	
   128	def test_the_coarser_measure_is_null_on_every_finer_row_while_the_key_is_not(scratch: Db):
   129	    """The mechanism rather than the number. A typed NULL is what keeps sum() additive across
   130	    grains -- and the KEY must fan out where the measure must not, which is the whole
   131	    distinction the bridge exists to draw."""
   132	    carried = _total(scratch, f"{OCCURRED} AND _measure__parent__size_parents_units IS NOT NULL")
   133	    assert carried == 0, "a child row carries no parent measure"
   134	    inherited = _total(scratch, f"{OCCURRED} AND parent_key IS NOT NULL")
   135	    assert inherited == 3, "and every child row does carry its parent's key"
   136	
   137	
   138	def test_the_parents_total_does_not_move_when_a_parent_gains_children(scratch: Db):
   139	    """The falsifiable half: change only the child count and the parent total must not move."""
   140	    before = _total(scratch, TOTAL)
   141	    _load(scratch, [(f"C{n}", "P1", Decimal("5.00")) for n in range(4, 9)])
   142	    _build(scratch)
   143	    after = _total(scratch, TOTAL)
   144	    assert after == before == Decimal("150.75")
   145	
   146	
   147	def test_the_trap_this_does_not_close_is_the_one_on_the_peripheral(scratch: Db):
   148	    """ADR 0012. The bridge protects the measure column and not the attribute beside it.
   149	
   150	    Asserted rather than lamented, because it is the half of D-0001's argument that is false
   151	    and a reader who trusts the entry needs to meet it here rather than in a report.
   152	    """
   153	    trapped = _total(
   154	        scratch,
   155	        "SELECT sum(p.parent_size) FROM dar__uss._bridge AS b "
   156	        "INNER JOIN dar__uss.parent AS p ON b.parent_key = p.parent_key "
   157	        "WHERE b._event = 'occurred'",
   158	    )
   159	    assert trapped == Decimal("251.25"), (
   160	        "summing the peripheral's attribute multiplies it once per child -- 100.50 twice and "
   161	        "50.25 once. The measure column returns 150.75 for the same shape"
   162	    )

# What the source sends, what it is called here, and what type it becomes. This file is the
# documentation, the schema and the transformation; there is nothing beside it to keep in
# step. Descriptions stay in the source's vocabulary -- what a thing MEANS is dab/model.yaml's
# job, and saying it twice is how two numbers start disagreeing.
endpoints:
  source:
    provider: odata
    service: https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1
    entity: OrderDetails
    page_size: 100  # the service rejects $top above 100 with a bare 400
  target:
    platform: duckdb
    models: [historized, current]

ownership:
  team: adss
  upstream: >-
    A public demo OData service. No owner, no SLA and no change notification, so a failing
    contract check is the notification. The recording under das/fixtures is what every build
    reads; the scheduled live run is what says the recording has gone stale.

schema:
  # The first composite key this system has met. DAS records it as the source declares it --
  # two columns -- and the single key the modelling engine needs is composed in the mapping,
  # where a check compares it back against these two. ADR 0010.
  primary_keys: [order_id, product_id]
  columns:
    - source_path: OrderId
      target_name: order_id
      type: INTEGER
      mode: REQUIRED
      description: >-
        Edm.Int32. Half the entity key. The metadata does not mark it Nullable=false, unlike
        Order.OrderId, which it does.
    - source_path: ProductId
      target_name: product_id
      type: INTEGER
      mode: REQUIRED
      description: Edm.Int32. The other half of the entity key, and likewise not marked non-null.
    - source_path: UnitPrice
      target_name: unit_price
      type: DECIMAL
      precision: 18
      scale: 4
      mode: REQUIRED
      description: >-
        Edm.Decimal with Scale=Variable, Nullable=false. The scale is pinned here because the
        source does not pin it. This is the price on the line, which is not necessarily the
        product's current price.
    - source_path: Quantity
      target_name: quantity
      type: INTEGER
      mode: REQUIRED
      description: Edm.Int16, Nullable=false.
    - source_path: Discount
      target_name: discount
      type: DECIMAL
      precision: 18
      scale: 4
      mode: REQUIRED
      description: >-
        Edm.Single, Nullable=false -- a 32-bit float. Recorded as a decimal rather than a
        double because the vocabulary has no REAL, so neither is a transcription, and a NaN
        or an Infinity then fails at this cast rather than propagating into a measure that
        both of a question's answers would agree on. D-0002, ADR 0011.
=== mapping ===
# How one entity is loaded from what the system recorded. This is the one artefact whose job
# is to bind two vocabularies, so it names both -- but only in table, primary_keys and
# transformation_expression. See docs/conventions.md section 1.4.
entity_id: ORDER_LINE
mapping_groups:
  - name: default_mapping_group
    tables:
      - connection: dev
        table: das__staged.order_details
        # The first composite key here. One entry, joined with || and a separator: `concat`
        # ignores nulls and would turn a missing half into a shorter key that collides with a
        # real one. A generated check counts this against the source's own two columns.
        # ADR 0010.
        primary_keys: ["cast(order_id AS VARCHAR) || '-' || cast(product_id AS VARCHAR)"]
        ingestion_strategy: FULL_LOG
        entity_effective_timestamp_expression: extracted_at
        attributes:
          - id: LINE_NUMBER
            transformation_expression: cast(order_id AS VARCHAR) || '-' || cast(product_id AS VARCHAR)
          - {id: QUANTITY, transformation_expression: quantity}
          - {id: AGREED_UNIT_PRICE, transformation_expression: unit_price}
          - {id: DISCOUNT_RATE, transformation_expression: discount}
          # Arithmetic over columns of this row, which M5 permits and ADR 0007 bounds.
          - id: REVENUE
            transformation_expression: quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)
    relationships:
      - id: ORDER_LINE_IS_PART_OF_ORDER
        source_table: das__staged.order_details
        # Spelled exactly as order-mapping.yaml spells its own key -- a bare column.
        # A cast here would produce a different VARCHAR and join to nothing.
        target_transformation_expression: order_id

+        An order is made of these, and this is where what was actually bought is recorded --

+          type: STRING

+        - id: QUANTITY

+          type: NUMBER

+        - id: AGREED_UNIT_PRICE

+            What was agreed when the order was accepted, which is not what the goods cost
+            today and does not move when the price does. It is the price before any discount.
+          type: NUMBER
+          effective_timestamp: true
+
+        - id: DISCOUNT_RATE
+          name: DISCOUNT_RATE
+          definition: The proportion of the agreed price the business gave up on this line.
+          description: >-
+            A proportion, not a percentage and not an amount: 0.25 means a quarter off. Zero

+          type: NUMBER
+          effective_timestamp: true
+
+        - id: REVENUE
+          name: REVENUE
+          definition: What the business took for this line, after the discount it gave up.

+          effective_timestamp: true

   # compile. Writing `type: "1:N"` here would read as a statement the engine never receives.
@@ -131,3 +185,12 @@ model:

       source_entity_id: ORDER
       target_entity_id: CUSTOMER
+
+    - name: IS_PART_OF
+      definition: The order this line is one of the things asked for on.
+      description: >-
+        A line belongs to exactly one order and to the same one for its whole life. It is also
+        where the line gets its date: a line has no day of its own, and the day it was asked
+        for is the day the order was accepted. ADR 0009.
+      source_entity_id: ORDER_LINE
+      target_entity_id: ORDER
diff --git a/dab/uss.yaml b/dab/uss.yaml
index 7508ff9..88e809e 100644
--- a/dab/uss.yaml
+++ b/dab/uss.yaml
@@ -53,3 +53,21 @@ uss:
             same set -- a division a question does, and never a number this system stores.
           aggregate: sum
           attribute: SHIP_LAG_DAYS
+
+    - id: ORDERED
+      entity: ORDER_LINE
+      definition: >-
+        A line was ordered: the business agreed to supply one kind of goods, in a quantity, at
+        a price. One per line, on the day the order carrying it was accepted -- a line has no
+        day of its own.
+      kind: transaction
+      # Inherited along IS_PART_OF, resolved with the key and at the same instant. ADR 0009.
+      date_attribute: ORDER.PLACED_ON
+      measures:
+        - id: REVENUE_ORDER_LINES_AMOUNT
+          definition: >-
+            What the business took, added up over lines. It is additive over any set of lines
+            and any period, because each line contributes what it earned exactly once -- and
+            it may not be added to anything measured per order, which is a different grain.
+          aggregate: sum
+          attribute: REVENUE

+"""One measure is non-null on its own event's rows and nowhere else, asserted on the real build.
+
+`tests/test_fan_out.py` proves the property on a warehouse it builds itself, with numbers. This
+is the same property stated as a mechanism and carried into every build: a measure that appeared
+on another event's rows would be summed there, and the sum would still look like a number.
+
+The distinction that matters here is EVENT and not stage. Two events on one entity share a stage
+-- a parent that happened and a parent that finished are both `_stage = 'parent'` -- so a check
+written per stage would let one of them carry the other's measure and report nothing. Every test
+below that could pass under a per-stage check is marked.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import pytest
+
+from adss.checks import measure_check_names, measure_checks
+from adss.model import read_model
+from adss.uss import read_uss
+
+Db = duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection
+
+FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "dab"
+
+SIZE = "_measure__parent__size_parents_units"
+HAPPENED = "_measure__parent__happened_parents_count"
+FINISHED = "_measure__parent__finished_parents_count"
+WEIGHT = "_measure__child__weight_children_units"
+
+COLUMNS = (HAPPENED, SIZE, FINISHED, "_measure__child__occurred_children_count", WEIGHT)
+
+
+def declarations():
+    model = read_model(FIXTURES / "model.yaml")
+    return model, read_uss(FIXTURES / "uss.yaml", model)
+
+
+def checks() -> dict[str, str]:
+    return measure_checks(declarations()[1])
+
+
+def warehouse(connection: Db) -> None:
+    """The bridge a measure check reads, empty. Stage and event are separate columns."""
+    connection.execute("CREATE SCHEMA dar__uss")
+    measures = ", ".join(f"{column} DECIMAL(28, 8)" for column in COLUMNS)
+    connection.execute(
+        f"CREATE TABLE dar__uss._bridge (_stage VARCHAR, _event VARCHAR, {measures})"
+    )
+
+
+def row(connection: Db, stage: str, event: str, **values: object) -> None:
+    held = [values.get(column) for column in COLUMNS]
+    marks = ", ".join(["?"] * (len(COLUMNS) + 2))
+    connection.execute(f"INSERT INTO dar__uss._bridge VALUES ({marks})", [stage, event, *held])
+
+
+def answer(connection: Db, column: str) -> int:
+    body = "\n".join(
+        line
+        for line in checks()[f"{column.removeprefix('_')}__isolated"].splitlines()
+        if not line.lstrip().startswith("--")
+    )
+    found = connection.execute(body).fetchone()
+    assert found is not None
+    return int(found[0])
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def scratch(tmp_path: Path) -> Iterator[Db]:
+    connection = duckdb.connect(str(tmp_path / "scratch.duckdb"))
+    warehouse(connection)
+    yield connection
+    connection.close()
+
+
+def test_there_is_one_check_per_measure_named_for_the_column_it_protects():
+    written = checks()
+    _, uss = declarations()
+    for _, _, column in uss.measure_columns():
+        assert f"{column.removeprefix('_')}__isolated" in written
+    assert len(written) == len(uss.measure_columns()), "no measure is checked twice or not at all"
+    assert set(measure_check_names(uss)) == {f"{name}.sql" for name in written}
+
+
+def test_a_measure_on_its_own_events_rows_and_nowhere_else_is_not_a_leak(scratch: Db):
+    row(scratch, "parent", "happened", **{HAPPENED: 1, SIZE: 100})
+    row(scratch, "parent", "finished", **{FINISHED: 1})
+    row(scratch, "child", "occurred", **{WEIGHT: 5})
+    for column in COLUMNS:
+        assert answer(scratch, column) == 0, column

+

+    """The fan-out shape: the child row carries the parent's size, and summing doubles it."""
+    row(scratch, "parent", "happened", **{HAPPENED: 1, SIZE: 100})
+    row(scratch, "child", "occurred", **{WEIGHT: 5, SIZE: 100})

+
+

+    """A per-STAGE check cannot see this one: both rows are `_stage = 'parent'`.
+
+    It is the likelier defect of the two -- one entity with two events is what slice 3 built,
+    and every branch of the union comes off the same stage's CTE.
+    """

findings.title: ADR 0002's excuse for three slices without the fan-out proof is false: the test passes unmodified on slice 2 and slice 3
findings.detail:
The paragraph rewritten this slice says: "**The fan-out test exists as of slice 4**, in `tests/test_fan_out.py`. It needs two grains — parents and children — so it could not be written while there was one entity, and this section said so through three slices rather than claiming a check nobody had written." tests/test_fan_out.py:4 repeats it: "Slices 1 to 3 could not demonstrate it -- every entity was at one grain".

The test touches none of the repository's real entities. It reads tests/fixtures/dab/model.yaml and tests/fixtures/dab/uss.yaml, creates its own dab."view_PARENT_hist" / dab."view_CHILD_hist" / dab."v_CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT" tables, inserts two parents and three children, and runs bridge_sql/peripheral_sql over them. That neutral fixture has had PARENT and CHILD, the many-to-one CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT edge, and measures on both grains since slice 2 (commit cee95ff); neither fixture file is touched by this slice's diff.

I checked this rather than argued it. I made git worktrees at claude/adss-slice-02-... and claude/adss-slice-03-..., copied slice 4's tests/test_fan_out.py in with no other change, and ran it: 5 passed on both. That includes test_the_trap_this_does_not_close_is_the_one_on_the_peripheral, the 251.25 assertion ADR 0012 presents as slice 4's discovery.

What is genuinely new in slice 4 is the measurement on real data — 2,155 real line rows, freight that does not move, 207,306.10 on the peripheral. That part is honest. The claim that the structural test was impossible earlier is not.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is the standing excuse for D-0001 — the deviation that puts every process into one shared dar__uss — having been carried on assertion for three slices, and deviations.md's Review section leans on the same reasoning ("slice 2 built the first edge but both its entities were at one grain, so the walk was exercised and the property was not"). A reader is told the proof was unavailable; it was available from slice 2 with the fixture that already existed. That turns a two-slice gap in verification into an apparently unavoidable one, which is exactly the true-sounding excuse the register's own Review clause exists to catch.

findings.title: ADR 0012's "all four mutations fail the suite" is false for one of the four; that mutation leaves the suite fully green
findings.detail:
The Confirmation ends: "Four mutations of the refusal were run and all four fail the suite." Commit 5a56849 names them: "doing nothing, ignoring windows, allowing an empty aggregate, and looking at only the first of an aggregate's columns. All four fail the suite."

The fourth does not. I changed src/adss/question.py:165 from

    loose = [column for column in columns if MEASURE not in column]

to

    loose = [column for column in columns[:1] if MEASURE not in column]

and ran the whole suite: 199 passed, zero failures. (I then restored the file; the tree is clean.) The other three do fail — "ignoring windows" fails test_a_windowed_aggregate_over_a_peripherals_column_is_refused as claimed.

The reason it cannot fail is structural: every aggregate anywhere in the repository has exactly one column. I parsed all five uss.sql files and all five synthetic answer queries in tests/test_questions.py through aggregated() — sum over one column each, and count(*) over none. No test or question ever puts two columns inside one aggregate, so columns[:1] and columns are indistinguishable.

The mutation is not harmless. Under it, sum(b._measure__parent__size_parents_units * p.parent_size) is accepted: the parse tree gives that aggregate the columns ('b._measure__parent__size_parents_units', 'p.parent_size'), the measure is first, and the peripheral column that multiplies with the fan-out is never inspected. That is exactly the trap ADR 0012 exists to refuse.
findings.why_it_matters: This slice also added a rule to .claude/skills/adss/SKILL.md: "Run the mutation before the ADR's Confirmation section claims one. A confirmation that names a test which could not fail for the reason given is worse than none, because it stops anybody looking again — and it has happened here more than once." The ADR written in the same slice does the thing the skill was written to stop. A reader who trusts line 156 will not add the missing multi-column test case, so the one genuine hole in the refusal stays open behind a confirmation that says it is closed.

findings.title: ADR 0009's Confirmation describes a data check on inherited dates that does not exist
findings.detail:
The Confirmation closes with: "A data check asserts that every bridge row's `_event_date` for such a stage equals the inherited entity's own date for the key on that row — the property that would break silently if the two were ever resolved at different instants."

There is no such check. checks/ holds 18 generated .sql files and `grep -rl "_event_date" checks/` returns nothing. src/adss/checks.py generates exactly three families — relationship_checks (one_target / loaded / resolves), composed_key_checks, measure_checks — plus the contract-level __clock and __key checks from src/adss/das.py; none compares a bridge date to a parent's date. run_checks has no inline assertion for it either. `uv run adss check` prints 43 findings and not one concerns _event_date.

What does exist is tests/test_uss.py:509-540, which substring-asserts that the date and key come out of the same CTE in the emitted text. That is a machinery test over generated SQL, not a data check over the built warehouse, and the ADR's own sentence distinguishes them: it stands as a separate final paragraph after the tests/test_uss.py one, claiming a property asserted on the warehouse in the sense checks/README.md defines.

The named property is the one this ADR calls the whole risk: its Decision Outcome argues that resolving the date at a different instant from the key "would put two instants on one bridge row, which is the confusion ADR 0006 calls the entire difference between the option it chose and the one it rejected."
findings.why_it_matters: A Confirmation section is what a later maintainer reads to know which properties survive a refactor of the generator. Claiming a build-time check for the one failure the ADR calls silent means nobody adds it — and a regression in _inherit_cte's as-of join (dated.eff_tmstp <= revision._observed_at) would ship with all 43 checks green and both of q04's answers agreeing, because the control query in staged.sql joins on order_id with no history at all and cannot see an as-of error.

    CAST('0.99999' AS DECIMAL(18,4))  ->  1.0000      -- rounded, no error

Both halves of the sentence are in fact discharged by one assertion in the other file, tests/test_das_sql.py:40-42, where test_every_type_in_the_vocabulary_emits_its_own_expression requires the string `cast(landed.payload ->> '$.ParentAmount' AS DECIMAL(18, 4)) AS parent_amount`. The property is covered; the citation is not.
findings.why_it_matters: It reads as two independent confirmations at two layers when there is one assertion in one file. Somebody narrowing or removing that single line in test_das_sql.py would leave the ADR still claiming a second guard in test_contract.py, and the precision and scale carried by the contract — which is what D-0002 rests on — would be unpinned with the record saying otherwise.

findings.title: ADR 0009 says the neutral fixture gained the inherited-date event; a separate fixture was added instead, so that SQL is never linted or executed
findings.detail:
"The neutral fixture gains an event on `CHILD` dated by `PARENT.HAPPENED_ON`, which is the shape this record is about and which the fixture did not have."

The neutral fixture is not touched: git diff over the slice shows no change to tests/fixtures/dab/uss.yaml or tests/fixtures/dab/model.yaml. A new file tests/fixtures/dab/inherited_date.yaml was added — a copy of the neutral uss.yaml with a fourth event appended — and only tests/test_uss.py reads it.

The difference is not cosmetic, because the neutral fixture is what the two executing consumers read:

- tests/test_generated_sql_lints.py:31 builds its emitters from dab/uss.yaml, so the inherited-date bridge SQL is never run through sqlfluff.
- tests/test_fan_out.py:89 reads dab/uss.yaml, so the inherited-date bridge SQL is never executed against a warehouse in the suite.

Everything asserted about the inherited date in tests/test_uss.py is a substring match on emitted text — including the as-of predicate and the `WHERE … _event_date IS NOT NULL` filter. That is the technique tests/test_fan_out.py's own docstring rejects: "A substring assertion would pass a generator that emitted the right typed nulls in the wrong branch."
findings.why_it_matters: Had the sentence been true, the inherited-date shape would have inherited the fixture's existing coverage for free — linted by test_generated_sql_lints and executed end to end by test_fan_out — and the ADR is written as if it did. As it stands the only execution of that code path is the real build, where adss check compares q04's two answers; and q04's control query joins order_details to orders on order_id with no history, so it cannot disagree with an as-of resolution error in _inherit_cte.
